chapter_theme: Severe pure Saivism (கடுஞ் சுத்த சைவம்): beyond outward signs, the severe pure Saiva destroys desire, bond and the state of a bound soul, strips away the tattvas and maya, and becomes pure Siva, until 'I' and 'He' can no longer be said and the senses are stilled in union.
structure_note: Two verses define the severe pure Saiva and the Siddhanta path by what is removed (1438, 1439), one by what is reached (1440), and two speak in the first person and of the result (1441, 1442), linked end to beginning by சாற்று.

1438.reading: Those who go beyond outward garb to Siva's side without show, crush the bonds of desire and lay waste bondage and the state of a bound soul, are the pure Saivas who know Siva.
1438.nuance: வேடம், garb, is the outward dress and signs of a sect, such as those of 1423 and 1424. பசுத்துவம் is the soul's state of being bound, not the soul itself. விகிர்தன், a name of Siva, is the one unlike all others. சிவபோதகர் may be those who know Siva or those who teach him.

1439.reading: To strip away the five that make the body, the six and the five, great maya in its layers and the rest, wipe away the bond of the isolated state and firmly reach oneself: that is the path of Siddhanta.
1439.nuance: ஐந்து, ஆறு and ஐந்து are traditionally groups of tattvas (elements, and the higher categories), stripped from the grossest upward. கேவலம் is in Siddhanta the soul's state wrapped in anava alone, before it takes a body; tradition supplies that sense. தனையுறல் may be reaching oneself or reaching Him.

1440.reading: Those who, without dwelling on words about pure Siva, reach the root that is the seed of release and the goal of the freed, and as souls so reach Hara that the separate self is gone, become pure Siva: they are the pure Saivas.
1440.nuance: அற்றால் (when it ceases) is read of the soul's separateness; tradition holds that the soul is not destroyed, and the verse does not say. Line 1 (சுத்தச் சிவனுரை தானத்தில் தோயாமல்) is obscure.

1441.reading: Searching out what 'I' is and what 'He' is, I came to the state of That where there are not two, He and I; since that truth was granted, I can no longer speak of He and I.
1441.nuance: The verse is a report of experience in the first person. தான் is the Lord here, and தற்பதம் may be 'the That-state' (tat) or 'his own state'. நல்கலால் (because it was given) makes the knowledge a gift, not an achievement.

1442.reading: When the truth beyond speech is attained, the five that are hard to curb subside, knowledge shines above as the light of a lamp, and union with the Supreme becomes one's station.
1442.nuance: சாற்றரிதாகிய (hard to speak of) picks up சாற்றகில்லேன் from 1441. The five are traditionally the senses. சாயுச்சியம் is union, the last of the four stations (salokya, samipya, sarupya, sayujya); பதி may be 'station' or 'the Lord'.

links.note: The Kural says the senses must be crushed as part of renouncing; Tirumular says the five, hard to curb, subside once the truth beyond speech is attained. The same subduing is a task in one and a result in the other.
Both cut the bonds of desire by turning to the Lord: the Kural by clinging to the one without clinging, Tirumular by going to Siva's side and crushing ஆசாபாசம்.
The Kural ends the pride of 'I' and 'mine' between a person and his goods; Tirumular ends the speech of 'I' and 'He' between the soul and the Lord. Both close with the 'I' given up.

source_issues: 1440: line 1 (சுத்தச் சிவனுரை தானத்தில் தோயாமல்) is obscure and may be corrupt.
